validity.recommendation: Keep the row. IGAT 2 is a real, correctly-classified gas transmission trunk and is NOT a duplicate of any other roster PID.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: unambiguously real. IGAT 2 (second Iran Gas Trunkline / khatt-e serasari-ye dovvom) is one of Iran's flagship gas trunklines, documented in the scholarly Encyclopaedia Iranica ('a 56-inch second trunkline' fed by the Kangan and Nar onshore fields) and in an independent commercial GIS product (digital-oil-gas-map) that maps the route with 3,138 turning points and 10 refinery/compressor stations. This is NOT a case where the only trace is GEM-derived. NOTE the gem.wiki page's own citations are thin/generic: only (1) a Wikipedia 'Iran Gas Trunkline' link and (2) a journal article about the Polkalleh compressor station — neither is a strong standalone source naming IGAT 2's specs, which is why this row needed independent re-corroboration. CLASSIFICATION: correct — a high-pressure 56-inch long-distance gas transmission trunk (not gathering/feeder, not oil/NGL, not plant-internal). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 31-row Iran gas operating roster and the GulfPub Iran gas list. GulfPub's own 'IGAT 2' (Kangan NG Refinery->Qazvin, 56 in, 640 km) is the same physical line = a corroborating match, not a separate GEM row. Distinct from P0443 IGAT 3 (Asaluyeh->Markazi) despite an identical copy-pasted capacity (see spec entry). GulfPub's separate 'IGAT 2 extension' (Qazvin->Tabriz, 48 in, 274 km) and 'IGAT 10' (Bushehr->Saveh) are different lines, not duplicates of this row. No duplicate concern.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify LengthKnown. GEM's 680 km is almost certainly too short; independent GIS + geography point to ~1,039 km. Also verify Capacity 32.85 bcm/y (likely copy-pasted from IGAT 3).
validity.researcher_notes: LENGTH — material disagreement. GEM = 680 km; GulfPub = 640 km; but the independent digital-oil-gas-map GIS dataset (a measured route, 3,138 turning points) gives 1,039 km (1,034 km horizontal), and Persian industry sources (infosaba, fa.wikipedia — surfaced via search, could not be cited: infosaba times out to bots, fa.wiki length token not in raw HTML) also state 1,039 km. Geography is decisive: Kangan/Fajr-Jam on the Bushehr coast (~27.8 N) to Qazvin (~36.3 N) is ~950 km straight-line, so a routed pipeline of ~1,039 km is right and 680 km (let alone 640) is physically impossible for this corridor. GEM 680 and GulfPub 640 likely both trace to an old partial-length figure. Recommend correcting LengthKnown to ~1,039 km. DIAMETER 56 in — CONFIRMED (Iranica '56-inch second trunkline'; GulfPub 56; digital-oil-gas-map 56; fa sources 56). CAPACITY — GEM = 32.85 bcm/y, which is IDENTICAL to P0443 IGAT 3's 32.85 (copy-paste red flag). Iranica gives the anticipated transfer rate of the 56-inch second trunkline as 'about 30 billion cubic meters per year'; original design was ~17 bcm/y export + ~10 bcm/y domestic. 32.85 is in the ballpark but unverified and suspiciously duplicated from IGAT 3 — treat as low confidence, verify before relying on it. FuelSource 'Nar and Kangan fields' — CONFIRMED (Iranica; Fajr-e-Jam/Kangan refinery treats Nar and Kangan onshore-field gas).

validity.recommendation: Change StartState/Province from 'Fars' to 'Bushehr'; consider naming the operator as National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC/IGTC) rather than only the Ministry of Petroleum.
validity.researcher_notes: START PROVINCE — GEM says 'Kangan Refinery, Fars'. The Kangan/Fajr-e-Jam gas refinery complex (Bandar Kangan / Jam) is administratively in BUSHEHR province, not Fars. Multiple independent sources place the origin refinery and the Nar/Kangan source fields in Bushehr province (Fajr-e-Jam refinery is in Bushehr; en.wikipedia 'constructed between Fajr Jam Refinery in Bushehr province and Qazvin'). There is a genuine historical ambiguity — older/Iranica text describes the Kangan and Nar fields as 'south of Fars Province near the shores of the Persian Gulf' (pre-Bushehr-boundary framing) — but by current administrative geography the correct province is Bushehr. END = Qazvin, Qazvin province: CONFIRMED. OWNER/OPERATOR — GEM lists Owner = Iran Ministry of Petroleum 100%, which is defensible as ultimate state owner, but the operating entity for the IGAT trunklines is the National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) / its Iranian Gas Transmission Company (IGTC) subsidiary. GulfPub tags the operator as NIOC, which is wrong for a domestic gas trunkline — do NOT adopt GulfPub's NIOC. Lesser caveat, not existence-level.

fills.researcher_notes: 56-inch diameter corroborated by Iranica ('56-inch second trunkline'), the digital-oil-gas-map GIS dataset (56 in), GulfPub (56), and Persian sources. High confidence.

Iranica states NIGC used non-associated gas from the Kangan and Nar onshore fields for the 56-inch second trunkline; the Fajr-e-Jam (Kangan) gas refinery (iranoilgas company page) treats Nar and Kangan field gas and is IGAT 2's origin. Two independent sources agree.

IGAT 2 is a long-standing operating trunkline (in service for decades); the GIS dataset maps it as an existing built line with 10 compressor/refinery stations and Iranica describes the trunkline network as operational. Status = operating confirmed at medium tier.

Endpoints Kangan/Fajr-e-Jam refinery -> Qazvin corroborated by the digital-oil-gas-map route product and Iranica/GulfPub. NOTE the province value is corrected here from GEM's 'Fars' to 'Bushehr' (the Kangan/Fajr-e-Jam complex is in Bushehr province) — see the attribution validity entry. End province Qazvin confirmed.

routes.start_name: Kangan / Fajr-e-Jam Gas Refinery, Bushehr province, Iran
routes.end_name: Qazvin (Qazvin compressor station), Qazvin province, Iran
routes.corridor_desc: The line runs from the Kangan/Fajr-e-Jam gas refinery complex on the Bushehr Persian Gulf coast (which processes Nar and Kangan onshore-field gas) generally northward up the central Zagros/Iranian plateau to the Qazvin compressor station in Qazvin province, feeding the northern demand region. Total routed length ~1,039 km per the independent digital-oil-gas-map GIS dataset (3,138 turning points, 1,034 km horizontal), consistent with the ~950 km straight-line separation. Endpoints are well-sourced and the two anchor coordinates below are real city/complex coordinates (Bandar Kangan; Qazvin city). Intermediate corridor is only loosely bounded here — it traverses Bushehr, Fars and Isfahan provinces before reaching Qazvin, and a precise 3,138-point route exists commercially (digital-oil-gas-map) but its coordinates are not in hand, so no interior waypoint coordinates are asserted (none fabricated).
routes.researcher_notes: Sheet currently has start='Asia'/end='Asia' and a RouteNotes image link only — effectively no usable route. Established real endpoints from the digital-oil-gas-map route product (Fajr-e-Jam/Kangan refinery -> Qazvin compressor station) and Iranica (Kangan/Nar source, second trunkline to the north). Start coordinate = Bandar Kangan town (~27.84 N, 52.06 E); end coordinate = Qazvin city (~36.28 N, 50.0 E) — both real, well-known place coordinates, not fabricated. No interior waypoint coordinates invented; corridor described in prose only. Suggested accuracy = medium (endpoints high-confidence, interior corridor loosely bounded).

summary: IGAT 2 real + correctly classified + not a duplicate; concerns: LENGTH 680 km almost certainly wrong (independent GIS + geography -> ~1,039 km), START PROVINCE 'Fars' should be 'Bushehr', and CAPACITY 32.85 bcm/y unverified & copy-pasted from IGAT 3.
